question.text: A circular coil of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is placed in a uniform magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> with its plane perpendicular to the field initially. It is rotated at constant angular speed about an axis along the diameter of coil and perpendicular to magnetic field so that it undergoes half of rotation in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The maximum value of EMF induced (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>μV</mi></math>) in the coil will be close to the integer....

solution.text:
Flux as a function of time ϕ=B→·A→=ABcos(ωt)

Emf induced,

e=-dϕdt=ABωsin(ωt)

Max. value of Emf = ABω

=πR2Bω

=3.14×0.1×0.1×3×10-5×π0.2=15
